title: Question about Map Sprites for Rpg maker Mz

posts.author: adam4landry
posts.body: Hi everyone I have a question about map sprites for rpg maker mz, I have heard that they are a lot of fun style of map sprites but I don’t know which style is more popular now i am curious which ones would be better for my project i am working on can anyone recommend any good sprites styles????

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
Does it matter what is "popular"? Why don't you pick whatever style you like most?
Or, give us some more details about your game, or show us a few pictures of what you like, and then ask here what we would prefer.

posts.author: Nirriti
posts.body:
Ideally you have an aesthetic vision for what you seek before starting. Ex:
"I'd like my game to look/feel like Super Mario RPG (snes)."
Basically acts as a guiding principle and things flows from there. Look them up, check countless, if unsure. One will click with you and get your creativity rolling.

Itch.io > Browse
(top left)
> Assets.
To the left, after that, theres
"types."
Pick
Tileset.
Note that as
@AquaEcho
said, its much easier to edit/make your own if you lower your scope of sprites. For example, Im going 8bit
(and im glad I did for the first project).
Makes it much easier to create/edit my tilesets. I spent countless hours reorganizing
(put the most used/important on top)
/recoloring a lot of it to my taste. Even making my characters
(map and battle sprites)
from scratch. <3 That said, theres plenty thats rich and gorgeous in 16 bit there too, if you want to.

Yes
(made a few for some furry fans even).
Though I only started making 8bit map sprites and battle sprites this year. 16BIT
(SNES)
while the same principles, requires way more efforts/considerations due to shadings
(which multiplies the time needed).
Map sprites are the easiest and more relaxed to make. First one is hard, but then all the rest will flow naturally as you use your first as a base of reference.
